name: Question 5
problem:
Find the fundamental vector product of the surface defined by the equations 

$$
x={u}^{2}+1,\,y={v}^{3}+1,\,z=2u+v.
$$
worked_solution:
For a surface with parametrization $r(u,v),$ the fundamental vector product is defined as ${r}_{u}^{′}\times {r}_{v}^{′}.$

In vector form, our surface has the equation 

$$
r(u,v)=⟨{u}^{2}+1,\,{v}^{3}+1,\,2u+v⟩.
$$

We first compute the tangent vectors to the grid curves:

$$
\begin{aligned}{r}_{u}^{′} & =⟨\frac{∂x}{∂u},\,\frac{∂y}{∂u},\,\frac{∂z}{∂u}⟩ \\  & =⟨\frac{∂}{∂u}({u}^{2}+1),\,\frac{∂}{∂u}({v}^{3}+1),\,\frac{∂}{∂u}(2u+v)⟩ \\  & =⟨2u,\,0,\,2⟩ \\ {r}_{v}^{′} & =⟨\frac{∂x}{∂v},\,\frac{∂y}{∂v},\,\frac{∂z}{∂v}⟩ \\  & =⟨\frac{∂}{∂v}({u}^{2}),\,\frac{∂}{∂v}({v}^{3}+1),\,\frac{∂}{∂v}(2u+v)⟩ \\  & =⟨0,\,3{v}^{2},\,1⟩\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the fundamental vector product is

$$
\begin{aligned}{r}_{u}^{′}\times {r}_{v}^{′} & =|\begin{aligned}i & j & k \\ 2u & 0 & 2 \\ 0 & 3{v}^{2} & 1\end{aligned}| \\  & =⟨|\begin{aligned}0 & 2 \\ 3{v}^{2} & 1\end{aligned}|,\,-|\begin{aligned}2u & 2 \\ 0 & 1\end{aligned}|,\,|\begin{aligned}2u & 0 \\ 0 & 3{v}^{2}\end{aligned}|⟩ \\  & =⟨-6{v}^{2},\,-2u,\,6u{v}^{2}⟩.\end{aligned}
$$

Question 5
?

Find the fundamental vector product of the surface defined by the equations

x=u2+1,y=v3+1,z=2u+v.

a
⟨v,−2u,−3uv2⟩
b
⟨v2−u,2v,uv2⟩
c
 ⟨u−v,2u,v2−u⟩
d
⟨−6v2+u,−2u+v,6uv2⟩
e
⟨−6v2,−2u,6uv2⟩
Submit
Correct
EXPLANATION

For a surface with parametrization r(u,v), the fundamental vector product is defined as ru′×rv′.

In vector form, our surface has the equation

r(u,v)=⟨u2+1,v3+1,2u+v⟩.

We first compute the tangent vectors to the grid curves:

ru′=⟨∂x∂u,∂y∂u,∂z∂u⟩=⟨∂∂u(u2+1),∂∂u(v3+1),∂∂u(2u+v)⟩=⟨2u,0,2⟩rv′=⟨∂x∂v,∂y∂v,∂z∂v⟩=⟨∂∂v(u2),∂∂v(v3+1),∂∂v(2u+v)⟩=⟨0,3v2,1⟩

Therefore, the fundamental vector product is

ru′×rv′=|ijk2u0203v21|=⟨|023v21|,−|2u201|,|2u003v2|⟩=⟨−6v2,−2u,6uv2⟩.
